correctness.rationale: The source gives a uniform chamber bound for every fixed labeled cyclic decomposition. A cyclic decomposition is a permutation of the vertex slots, and relabeling slots acts by conjugation. Conjugacy classes in the symmetric group are exactly cycle types. Because ordinary link components are unordered and unoriented, every link realization can be relabelled into a canonical decomposition with the same component-length partition. Thus one model per partition into parts at least three suffices. Multiplying the fixed-model bound by the restricted partition count and applying the Hardy--Ramanujan growth of the partition function gives the stated asymptotic exponent.

value.rationale: The refinement removes an entire factorial-scale overcount from the source's ordinary-link extension and makes the link upper exponent match the source's knot upper exponent. The mechanism is structural rather than cosmetic: it identifies the correct combinatorial parameter space as component-length cycle types, not all labeled cyclic decompositions. This is directly useful in asymptotic stick-complexity enumeration and isolates where any future improvement must come from after label redundancy is removed.
